title: Grade 4 CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — 3.8.2 Parable of the mustard seed

pages.lesson:
PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

In Luke 13:18-19 Jesus says the kingdom of God is like a mustard seed that a man planted. It grew and became a tree, and the birds perched in its branches. In this sub-strand you will retell that parable, see how God's kingdom grows from a small beginning, and learn how you can take part by living your faith and telling others.

## Strand 3.0: The Life of Jesus Christ
Sub-strand 3.8.2: Parable of the mustard seed
Suggested lessons: 3

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) retell the parable of the mustard seed as guided by the Bible text
b) describe how the kingdom of God grows from a small beginning
c) explain how they contribute to the growth of the kingdom of God
d) appreciate the growth of God’s kingdom by evangelising to others

## Key inquiry questions
1. How does the parable of the mustard seed relate to the kingdom of God?

## Core competencies
• Creativity and Imagination: the skill of communicating new ideas is enhanced as learners draw a big tree and compare it to the growth of God’s kingdom.
• Digital Literacy: the skill of digital citizenship is portrayed as learners watch a video clip on a mustard seed.

## Values
• Unity: is enhanced as learners work in groups to collect small seeds from the school compound.
• Responsibility: is enhanced as learners plant the seeds, water them and observe as the seeds sprout and grow to a big tree.

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Socio Economic Issues: environmental education is nurtured as learners plant the seeds, water them and observe as the seeds sprout and grow to a big tree.

## Links to other learning areas
• Agriculture: is enhanced as learners collect seeds and plant them.
• Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners draw, sing and role play.
• English: reading skills are enhanced as learners read the Bible.

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Christian Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 3.0 The Life of Jesus Christ, Sub-strand 3.8.2 Parable of the mustard seed
• Luke 13:18-19

PAGE 2: Lesson 1: The seed that became a tree

LESSON 1: THE SEED THAT BECAME A TREE
=====================================

## What you will learn
• Retell the parable of the mustard seed from Luke 13:18-19.
• Name the parts of the picture Jesus used.

Curriculum outcomes: a) retell the parable of the mustard seed as guided by the Bible text

## Introduction
A seed can look too small to matter. Jesus said the kingdom of God is like a seed a man planted. What looked small grew into a tree where birds could rest.

## Notes
Read Luke 13:18-19 and narrate it in Jesus' own order.

Jesus asked, "What is the kingdom of God like? What shall I compare it to?" Then He said it is like a mustard seed which a man took and planted in his garden. It grew and became a tree, and the birds of the air perched in its branches.

### The picture, part by part
- A man takes the seed. The kingdom is something God plants and people receive.
- He plants it in his garden. It is put into the soil on purpose, not thrown away.
- The seed is small at the start. The parable begins with a seed, not with a tree.
- It grows and becomes a tree. Growth is part of the story.
- Birds perch in its branches. The grown kingdom gives a resting place.

Do not add measurements or extra stories about the plant. The verses do not give a height or a number of years. They say it grew and became a tree, and birds perched in its branches.

You can watch a video clip about a mustard seed if the teacher provides one, and you can look at any small seed in the school compound. Use the seed to remember the parable. The lesson is not a science experiment by itself. It is Jesus' picture of the kingdom of God.

Draw the story in two parts if you wish: a hand planting a tiny seed, and a tree with birds. When you narrate, begin with Jesus' question, "What is the kingdom of God like?"

## Key words
• parable — a story Jesus told to teach a truth
• mustard seed — the small seed Jesus used as a picture of the kingdom of God
• kingdom of God — God's reign, His rule over those who belong to Him

## Activity: Read and draw the parable
You will need: Bible, Paper, Colours, Small seeds from the compound if the teacher allows
1. Read Luke 13:18-19 and narrate the parable.
2. In groups, collect small seeds from the school compound.
3. Look at how small a seed is, then draw a big tree with birds resting on its branches.
4. If a video clip on a mustard seed is available, watch it and say which part matches Jesus' words.

## Practice
1. What question did Jesus ask at the start of the parable?
2. What did the man do with the mustard seed?
3. What happened to the seed, and what did the birds do?

## Summary
• Jesus compared the kingdom of God to a mustard seed.
• A man planted it, and it grew into a tree.
• Birds perched in its branches.

### Answers to practice
1. What is the kingdom of God like? What shall I compare it to?
2. He planted it in his garden.
3. It grew and became a tree, and the birds perched in its branches.

PAGE 3: Lesson 2: From a small beginning

LESSON 2: FROM A SMALL BEGINNING
================================

## What you will learn
• Describe how the kingdom of God grows from a small beginning.
• Compare a growing seed with the growth of God's kingdom.

Curriculum outcomes: b) describe how the kingdom of God grows from a small beginning

## Introduction
Nobody looking only at a seed can see the tree. The kingdom of God also starts in a way that can look small, and then it grows.

## Notes
A beginning is the first stage. In the parable the beginning is a seed in a garden. The end of the picture is a tree with birds in the branches. Jesus says the kingdom of God is like that. It grows from a small beginning.

### How this helps us understand the kingdom
God's kingdom is His rule in the lives of people who trust and obey Him. It did not look large when Jesus told this parable to ordinary listeners. The picture promised growth. What God plants, He can make great.

The birds in the branches show that the grown kingdom is a place of rest and welcome. People find a home under God's rule.

### Watching growth
If you plant the small seeds you collected, water them and watch them, you are not changing the parable. You are seeing how a real seed sprouts. A sprout is still small. In time a healthy plant becomes much bigger than the seed. Environmental care matters here: do not waste water, do not uproot a classmate's plant, and do not leave litter in the garden. Responsibility is shown when you water what you planted.

Compare your drawing of the tree with the kingdom:

- The seed is the small start.
- The soil and water remind you that growth takes God's care and people's faithfulness.
- The tree is the kingdom grown large.
- The birds are those who find rest in it.

Do not claim the plant in the school garden is the kingdom. It is a picture, the way Jesus used the mustard seed as a picture. The kingdom grows by God's power as people believe and obey.

## Key words
• beginning — the first and small stage from which something grows
• sprout — the young growth that comes from a seed
• reign — God's rule as King

## Activity: Plant, water and compare
You will need: Small seeds, Soil in a tin or a corner of the school garden, Water, Exercise book
1. Plant the seeds, water them, and observe them as they sprout.
2. Draw a big tree with birds resting on its branches.
3. Write three sentences that compare the tree to the growth of God's kingdom.
4. Tell the class how the kingdom grows from a small beginning.

## Practice
1. What is the small beginning in the parable?
2. What does the tree with birds teach about the kingdom of God?
3. Is the plant in the school garden the same thing as God's kingdom?

## Summary
• The kingdom of God starts small, like a seed.
• It grows until it is like a tree.
• The birds show that the kingdom becomes a place of welcome and rest.

### Answers to practice
1. The mustard seed that the man planted.
2. God's kingdom grows from a small start and becomes a place where people can find rest.
3. No. It is a picture to help us understand the parable. The kingdom grows by God's power.

PAGE 4: Lesson 3: Taking part in the growth of the kingdom

LESSON 3: TAKING PART IN THE GROWTH OF THE KINGDOM
==================================================

## What you will learn
• Explain how a learner can contribute to the growth of God's kingdom.
• Appreciate that growth by telling other people about Jesus.

Curriculum outcomes: c) explain how they contribute to the growth of the kingdom of God; d) appreciate the growth of God’s kingdom by evangelising to others

## Introduction
A seed does not plant itself in the parable. A man planted it. Christians also have a part in the growth of God's kingdom. One part is telling others the good news.

## Notes
To contribute means to add your part. You do not make the kingdom grow by your own power. God gives the growth. You can still do the work He gives children.

### What you can do
- Believe in Jesus and obey Him at home and at school.
- Pray for other people.
- Join in church activities: singing, listening to the lesson, helping to keep the place tidy.
- Speak kindly so that people see a different way of living.
- Tell a friend what you have learnt about Jesus. That telling is evangelising, sharing the good news.
- Invite a friend to church or to Sunday school, with your parent's knowledge.
- Forgive, share and tell the truth. These actions show what God's rule looks like.

Role-play the activities you do in church: arriving, greeting, singing, listening, and helping. Then role-play a short conversation: "Jesus loves you. He wants you in God's kingdom." Keep the words true and simple.

### Responding to salvation
Salvation is being saved by Jesus. You respond when you believe Him, turn from sin, and follow Him. A person who has responded does not keep the news locked away. Appreciating the growth of the kingdom means you are glad when another person believes, just as the woman with the lost coin was glad, and you help that growth by evangelising.

Sing a song about the kingdom of God. Remember the seed. Your faithful word or kind act may look small. God is able to make it part of a great tree.

## Key words
• evangelise — to tell other people the good news about Jesus
• contribute — to add your part to a work
• salvation — being saved by Jesus

## Activity: Church work and good news
You will need: Space to role-play
1. Role-play the activities you do in church.
2. Say how you respond to salvation.
3. In pairs, practise telling a friend one true sentence about Jesus.
4. Sing a song about the kingdom of God.

## Practice
1. Name three ways a learner can contribute to the growth of God's kingdom.
2. What does evangelise mean?
3. Who makes the kingdom grow?

## Summary
• God gives the growth of His kingdom.
• Learners contribute by obeying, praying, serving in church and telling others about Jesus.
• Evangelising is sharing the good news.

### Answers to practice
1. Any three: believe and obey, pray, take part in church, live kindly, tell a friend about Jesus, invite someone to church, forgive and share.
2. To tell other people the good news about Jesus.
3. God. We add our part by believing, obeying and telling others.
pages.quiz:
REVISION QUIZ — 3.8.2 PARABLE OF THE MUSTARD SEED
========================================

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. The parable of the mustard seed in this sub-strand is:
   A. Luke 13:18-19
   B. Luke 15:8-10
   C. Mark 10:46-52
   D. Genesis 17:1-5

2. Jesus said the kingdom of God is like...
   A. a lost coin
   B. a mustard seed planted in a garden
   C. a roaring lion
   D. a tax collector

3. The seed grew and became...
   A. a stone
   B. a tree
   C. a river
   D. a city wall

4. The birds...
   A. perched in its branches
   B. ate the man
   C. stayed away forever
   D. planted more seeds in the story

5. The small beginning in the parable is...

6. The growth from seed to tree teaches that God's kingdom:
   A. never changes size
   B. grows from a small beginning
   C. is only a school plant
   D. ends when birds come

7. Planting seeds at school helps learners:
   A. replace the Bible story with a different meaning
   B. see a picture of growth and care for the environment
   C. avoid church
   D. measure God's kingdom in centimetres

8. A learner contributes to the kingdom when he or she:
   A. obeys God, prays and tells others about Jesus
   B. keeps the good news a secret forever
   C. mocks people who believe
   D. refuses to take part in church

9. To evangelise means...

10. Who gives the growth of the kingdom?
   A. Only the birds
   B. God
   C. A mustard plant by itself
   D. A crowd that never prays
pages.answers:
ANSWERS — 3.8.2 PARABLE OF THE MUSTARD SEED
========================================

1. A. Luke 13:18-19
   The class reads Luke 13:18-19.

2. B. a mustard seed planted in a garden
   Luke 13:19 gives this comparison.

3. B. a tree
   The parable says it grew and became a tree.

4. A. perched in its branches
   Luke 13:19 says the birds of the air perched in its branches.

5. The mustard seed.
   The kingdom is compared to the seed that later becomes a tree.

6. B. grows from a small beginning
   Jesus uses growth from a seed to a tree as the picture of the kingdom.

7. B. see a picture of growth and care for the environment
   The seeds are a picture and a way of caring for plants. They are not a new meaning.

8. A. obeys God, prays and tells others about Jesus
   Those actions are the learner's part in the growth of the kingdom.

9. To tell other people the good news about Jesus.
   The outcome asks learners to appreciate the kingdom by evangelising.

10. B. God
   Learners contribute, and God gives the growth.
